question: Identify a hydrocarbon pair that is NOT the part of the homologous series.
solution:
The correct answer is C4H4 and C5H10__**.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **A series of hydrocarbons** having **similar chemical properties** and **sharing the same general formula** constitute a **homologous series**. 
 
• Each member of a homologous series differs from the succeeding or preceding member by CH2.
 
• These organic compounds** have a similar structure and functional group**.
 
• The hydrocarbons in a homologous series **show a gradation in physical properties**.
 
• For example- CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈,... represent the homologous series of **alkanes** having general formula as **CₙH****₂ₙ₊₂****, **where n denotes the number of carbon atoms**. **Successive terms of the series differ by CH₂.
 
• Similarly, C₂H4, C3H6, C4H8,... represent the homologous series of **alkenes** having general formula as **CnH****2n**. Here also, the successive terms differ by CH2.
 
• Also, C₂H₂, C₃H₄, C₄H₆,... represent the homologous series of **alkynes **having general formula as **CₙH₂ₙ₋₂. **Again the successive terms differ by CH2.
 
• Clearly, **C2H6 and C3H9 are not part of the homologous series as they do not differ by the molecular formula of CH****2** but differ by CH3.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Characteristics of Homologous Series**

 
 
• **​**All members of a homologous series can be **represented by a** **general formula**.
 
• Each member of a homologous series **differs** **from its successive or preceding member** **by the molecular formula of CH****2**.
 
• Each member of a homologous series **differs from its successive or preceding member by the molecular mass of 14**.
 
• All members of a homologous series can be** prepared by the same general method**.
 
• All members of a homologous series have the** same chemical properties** due to the presence of the same functional group.
 
• Due to different molecular masses, members of a homologous series **show differences in physical properties** like melting point, boiling point, solubility, etc.** but with a gradation**.
